solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rebuilding a spire is something churchgoers do

indicators.note: rebuilding means putting something back together differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Restoring a church spire is a task the congregation takes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebuilding' rearranges the six letters of A SPIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Worshippers sing hymns of worship and glorify God, which is exactly what this word names.

clue.text: Tart has jewellery around tip of conk — in this?

definitions.text: Tart has jewellery around tip of conk — in this?

parts.note: a tart is a kind of pie

indicators.note: around says the jewellery word goes round the next piece

parts.note: a ring is a piece of jewellery

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A floozy wears a ring around her nose: is that a body ornament?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conk' is British slang for the nose. 'around' puts C inside RING after the I, giving RCING. The whole clue also describes a nose ring, the thing it defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose ring needs a hole made through the flesh, which is the body modification named.

clue.text: Surreptitiously foremost of ancient history professors read and copy books without authorisation

indicators.note: doing something surreptitiously means mixing it up out of sight, so the letters are jumbled
foremost of picks the first letter of each word that follows

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: History dons secretly read and duplicate books without permission.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of 'ancient history professors read and' give AHPRA; 'Surreptitiously' shuffles these with COPY.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical writings excluded from the accepted canon are those lacking official sanction as scripture.

clue.text: Irregularly liaise with PC for one part-time cop

indicators.note: irregularly means out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged
with PC for one means PC takes the place of a letter meaning one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A police constable, now and then, works alongside others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps one I of LIAISE for PC, giving LPCAISE; 'Irregularly' shuffles that.
explanation.definitionFit: A special constable is a volunteer British police officer who serves only some hours.

clue.text: Appreciate having completed run

definitions.meaning: to appreciate is to rise in value
in cricket a batsman who has finished a run is safely back behind the line, in the crease

explanation.surface: Value the satisfaction of finishing a run.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as IN CREASE: in cricket the crease is the line a batsman must reach to complete a run.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets that appreciate grow in worth, the verb sense of getting bigger.

clue.text: Blackleg covers entrance from which deliveries are made

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, covering it

parts.note: a blackleg works during a strike, so is a non-striker
to entrance is to send, delight or enrapture

explanation.surface: A strikebreaker guards the gate where supplies arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler delivers the ball from the end where the batsman not facing stands. 'Deliveries' suggests goods vans; it is bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket bowlers run in past the idle batsman's wicket, so that is the end they bowl balls from.

clue.text: Give more support to dispute around Albert Sq area

indicators.note: around says the dispute word encloses the area

parts.note: a row is a dispute
Albert Square is the setting of the soap EastEnders, in the East End of London, written E END

explanation.surface: A quarrel in a London square over who funds it.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running British TV soap set in Albert Square in London's East End, abbreviated E END.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to provide funds or backing; doing so again is renewed financial provision.

clue.text: A mostly unimportant sort of acid

indicators.note: mostly means losing the final letter of the word

parts.note: minor means unimportant

explanation.surface: A type of acid that hardly matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Proteins are built from these organic compounds, which a chemist calls a class of acids.

clue.text: Football team drawing with the Spanish on top

indicators.note: in a down clue the Spanish word sits above the other

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
a team drawing a game is level, even

explanation.surface: A soccer side ties, with Spaniards leading the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A soccer side fields this number of players, so the number names the team.

clue.text: Where Ulster is governed controls matters somehow excluding Republicans

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive by some unstated rearrangement
excluding means a letter is left out

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Northern Ireland's seat of power runs affairs without republicans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluding' drops an R from CONTROLS MATTERS; 'somehow' shuffles the remaining fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This Belfast building houses the Northern Ireland Executive, the seat of the province's devolved government.

clue.text: First lady holding fair draw

indicators.note: holding means the first word encloses the next

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis
OK means fair or satisfactory

explanation.surface: The president's wife hosts a fete with a raffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw out memories or a response is to call them forth, the same as summon up.

clue.text: Fruit: taste before tucking in at home

parts.note: a tang is a sharp taste

indicators.note: tucking in puts the home word inside the other

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
in means at home

explanation.surface: Sample the fruit before eating it at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' looks like an order signal for the charade, but it supplies a word of its own, and 'tucking in' fills that word with the home piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A small orange citrus related to the mandarin is this sort of produce.

clue.text: Jeweller about with more style

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
artier means more artistic, more stylish

explanation.surface: A goldsmith flaunting greater flair.
explanation.definitionFit: This Paris house is a famous firm of luxury watchmakers and gem merchants.

clue.text: What could develop into toad with 'elp

definitions.text: What could develop into toad with 'elp

indicators.note: develop into hints at change of form, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: help with the h dropped, as a Cockney might say it

explanation.surface: A young frog in need of a bit of help to grow up.
explanation.walkthrough: TOAD and ELP rearrange; the whole clue also defines it, since this creature grows into a toad.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva of frogs and toads hatches in water and matures into the adult amphibian.

clue.text: Clarion and weapons deployed in conflict

indicators.note: troops deployed are spread into new positions, so the letters are redistributed

explanation.surface: Bugles and arms brought into action in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' rearranges CLARION and WEAPONS.
explanation.definitionFit: These were the series of European battles of 1803 to 1815 against France, a war.

clue.text: It's dangerous entertaining you with hard spirit

indicators.note: entertaining means holding the others inside

parts.note: risky means dangerous
ye is an old form of you
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Hosting you with strong liquor is a hazardous business.
explanation.definitionFit: Distilled grain liquor of this kind is an alcoholic drink, known as a spirit.

clue.text: People making bets about first in race having lost shirt — and everything else!

definitions.text: having lost shirt — and everything else!

indicators.note: about says the bettors go round the next letter

parts.note: stakers are those placing stakes

indicators.note: first in picks the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Gamblers who backed a loser in the opening race have lost everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost shirt' is the gambler's idiom for losing everything, which nudges towards the surface story; it actually means naked.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for stark naked, wearing no clothing at all.

clue.text: An ordinary person entertains them hilariously

indicators.note: hilariously suggests wild comic disorder, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A regular bloke amuses the crowd to great laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hilariously' rearranges ENTERTAINS THEM; 'entertains' looks like a container signal but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom refers to a typical member of the public, the average citizen.

clue.text: Pressing suffering in groin

indicators.note: suffering means damaged or in distress, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Urgent treatment needed for a groin strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' suggests urgent; it is smoothing clothes with a hot iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes flattens creases with a hot appliance, the household chore.

clue.text: Digital security device

parts.note: digital here means of the finger: a sewing cap that protects a fingertip from the needle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' suggests computers; it means relating to a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal cap worn when sewing shields the fingertip, so it keeps a digit safe.

clue.text: Bleats could come from this

parts.note: both the noise of goats and sheep housed in a farm building, and a hint that rearranging the answer's letters spells the first word

explanation.surface: Baaing sounds might issue from this farm building.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: rearrange the answer and you get BLEATS. Animals housed here also bleat.
explanation.definitionFit: Livestock such as goats are kept in this farm building, and they make the noise.

clue.text: Draw instrument a doctor gets in

indicators.note: gets in means the doctor enters the instrument word

parts.note: a tool is an instrument
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A medic arrives bearing equipment to pick the winning ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: A raffle where tickets are pulled from a spinning drum is a kind of prize draw.

clue.text: Award most excellent Indian food

parts.note: ME stands for Most Excellent, an honorific title
dal is an Indian lentil dish

explanation.surface: A prize for the finest Indian cuisine.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal disc given for achievement or bravery is a decoration or prize.

clue.text: Move like a snake, sidewinder, extremely supple inside

indicators.note: inside puts the supple word between those letters
extremely picks the outermost letters of the word

parts.note: lithe means supple

explanation.surface: A sidewinder rattlesnake, very flexible, glides along.
explanation.walkthrough: A sidewinder is a desert rattlesnake, so it sits in the scene; here only its end letters count.
explanation.definitionFit: Serpents glide over the ground with a sliding, sinuous motion.

clue.text: Stately home with poor-quality china

parts.note: bad means poor in quality
Minton is a famous English porcelain maker

explanation.surface: A grand house fitted out with cheap porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: Badminton House is a Gloucestershire country seat, home of the Dukes of Beaufort; Minton is a Staffordshire pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: This ducal mansion in Gloucestershire is a grand English country house.

clue.text: One who played jazz live while one is entertained

indicators.note: is entertained says these pieces are held inside the live word

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
as means while
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A musician who performed jazz live while the audience was amused.
explanation.walkthrough: Count Basie was an American big-band jazz pianist and bandleader.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Basie led a famous swing band and played piano, a jazz musician.

clue.text: They mark passing that is in European Union records

indicators.note: in says the that-is abbreviation sits within the records

parts.note: logs are records
IE is id est, that is

explanation.surface: Brussels files that note the passage of new laws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passing' suggests legislation; it means death.
explanation.definitionFit: Funeral speeches praising the deceased commemorate someone's death.

clue.text: Taken in robbery — LSD, jewels

indicators.note: taken in says the letters are contained within the following words

explanation.surface: Jewels and cash in old pounds, shillings and pence seized in a heist.
explanation.walkthrough: LSD is pre-decimal British money: pounds, shillings and pence.
explanation.definitionFit: Green and blue gemstones such as emerald and aquamarine are varieties of this mineral.
